questions.question: Which of the following states has the lowest female literacy rate as per Census of India 2011?

• Improving female literacy is crucial for the overall development and empowerment of women in the state.

questions.question: Which is the oldest and most widespread industry in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Textile**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Textile industry** is the **oldest **and most widespread **industry **in India.
 
• It plays a significant role in the Indian economy by providing employment to millions and contributing substantially to the country's export earnings.
 
• The industry covers a wide range of activities from the production of raw materials like cotton, jute, silk, and wool, to the manufacturing of finished products like garments and apparels.
 
• India has a rich heritage of textiles, with a history that dates back to ancient times, when Indian textiles were highly sought after in international markets.
 
• The industry is known for its diverse range of products, including traditional handloom and handicraft items, as well as modern, machine-made fabrics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian textile industry** is one of the largest in the world, with a vast raw material base and manufacturing strength across the value chain.
 
• The industry contributes around **7% to India's industrial output** in value terms, **2% to the GDP, and 15% to the country's export earnings**.
 
• It is the second largest employer in the country after agriculture, employing over 45 million people directly and 60 million people indirectly.
 
• Government initiatives like the **Textile Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS)** and **Make in India** campaign have provided a significant boost to the sector.
 
• The sector is expected to reach **USD 300 billion by 2025** with a CAGR of 10%.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs is/are INCORRECTLY matched?

A. Separation of Executive from the Judiciary – Article 50

B. Organisation of the village panchayats and endow them with powers – Article 40

C. Promote justice, on a basis of equal opportunity, and to provide free legal aid to the poor – Article 39A

D. Organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines – Article 45
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**D only**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 50** deals with the Separation of Executive from the Judiciary.
 
• **Article 40** pertains to the Organisation of village panchayats and endows them with powers.
 
• **Article 39A** promotes justice on a basis of equal opportunity and provides free legal aid to the poor.
 
• **Article 45** originally dealt with the provision for free and compulsory education for children. However, it was amended, and the provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years was added.
 
• Therefore, the statement "Organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines" does not belong to Article 45, making it incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **directive to organize agriculture and animal husbandry** on modern and scientific lines is actually found in **Article 48** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The directive principles of state policy aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They also aim to establish social and economic democracy through a welfare state.
 
• While these principles are** non-justiciable**, they are fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

questions.question: When is the Constitution Day observed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**26 November**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Constitution Day**, also known as **Samvidhan Divas**, is observed on **26th November** every year in India.
 
• It commemorates the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949**.
 
• The day is marked by various events and activities that promote awareness about the Constitution and its significance.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **supreme law of the land** and provides the framework for governance, fundamental rights, and duties of citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India came into effect on **26th January 1950**, which is celebrated as **Republic Day**.
 
• It lays down the fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written constitution** of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic**, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• **Amendments **to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.

questions.question: ________ is an example of acoelomate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Platyhelminthes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Platyhelminthes** are commonly known as **flatworms**.
 
• They are characterized by their **simple, flattened, and unsegmented body structure**.
 
• Platyhelminthes are acoelomates, meaning they lack a body cavity (coelom) between the digestive tract and outer body wall.
 
• This phylum includes organisms such as **tapeworms and flukes**, which can be free-living or parasitic.
 
• Unlike other phyla, Platyhelminthes have a three-layered body plan but no specialized circulatory or respiratory systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acoelomates** are animals that do not possess a coelom, which is a fluid-filled cavity lined with mesoderm tissue.
 
• The lack of a coelom in Platyhelminthes limits their size and the complexity of their organ systems.
 
• They exhibit bilateral symmetry and have a simple gut with a single opening.
 
• Platyhelminthes play a significant role in medical and biological research due to their regenerative abilities and parasitic nature.

questions.question: The likelihood of a neutral atom gaining an electron is known as:
questions.solution:
The likelihood of a neutral atom gaining an electron is known as __**electron affinity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electron affinity** is defined as the amount of energy released when a neutral atom in the gaseous phase gains an electron to form a negative ion.
 
• This property is an indication of the** ability of an atom to accept an electron**.
 
• Higher electron affinity values indicate a greater tendency to gain an electron.
 
• Electron affinity generally increases across a period and decreases down a group in the periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electronegativity** is a measure of the tendency of an atom to attract a bonding pair of electrons.
 
• **Electro positivity** is the ability of an element to donate electrons and form positive ions.
 
• Electron affinity is different from electronegativity, which is a measure of the ability of an atom to attract electrons in a chemical bond.
 
• Elements with high electron affinities tend to be non-metals, as they are more likely to gain electrons.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true regarding Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022?

1. The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 1 Dec 2022.

2. The Bill seeks to give effect to the Antarctic Treaty, the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources and the Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty.

3. It also seeks to protect the Antarctic environment and regulate activities in the region.

4. The provisions of the Bill will apply to any person, vessel or aircraft that is a part of an Indian expedition to Antarctica under a permit issued under the Bill.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2, 3 and 4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 **was introduced in **Lok Sabha on 1 April 2022**, not 1 December 2022.
 
• The Bill seeks to give effect to the Antarctic Treaty, the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources, and the Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty.
 
• It also seeks to **protect the Antarctic environment **and regulate activities in the region.
 
• The provisions of the Bill will apply to any person, vessel, or aircraft that is a part of an Indian expedition to Antarctica under a permit issued under the Bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Antarctic Treaty was **signed in 1959 and came into force in 1961**, with the aim to ensure that Antarctica is used for peaceful purposes and scientific research.
 
• India became a party to the Antarctic Treaty in 1983 and has since established research stations in the region, including** 'Maitri' and 'Bharati'**.
 
• The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 is the first domestic legislation aimed at regulating Indian activities in Antarctica, ensuring compliance with international agreements.

questions.question: What is the name of the highest peak of Indian Garhwal Himalayas located in Chamoli district of Uttarakhand state with a height of 7,816 metres?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nanda Devi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nanda Devi** is the **highest peak of the Indian Garhwal Himalayas** located in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand state with a height of **7,816 metres**.
 
• It is the second highest mountain in India and the 23rd highest peak in the world.
 
• Nanda Devi is part of the Greater Himalayas and is renowned for its challenging climbing routes and breathtaking scenery.
 
• The Nanda Devi National Park, which surrounds the peak, is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and a popular destination for trekkers and nature enthusiasts.
 
• The first successful ascent of Nanda Devi was made by a British-American expedition in 1936.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Nanda Devi holds significant cultural and religious importance to the local communities in Uttarakhand.
 
• Due to its fragile ecosystem, the Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve was established to protect the region's unique flora and fauna.
 
• In 1982, the area was closed to climbers and trekkers to preserve its natural environment, although some parts have since been reopened under strict regulations.
 
• The peak is named after the Hindu goddess Nanda Devi, who is revered as the patron deity of the region.
 
• Efforts are continuously made to balance ecological preservation with sustainable tourism in the area.

questions.question: Which of the following cities was the capital of the Pallavas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanchipuram**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kanchipuram** was the capital city of the **Pallava dynasty**.
 
• The Pallavas ruled parts of South India from the **4th to the 9th centuries CE**.
 
• Kanchipuram is renowned for its architectural marvels, including the Kailasanathar Temple and the Vaikunta Perumal Temple.
 
• The city was also a significant center of learning and culture during the Pallava period, attracting scholars and artists from various parts of the country.
 
• The Pallavas contributed significantly to the development of Dravidian architecture, which influenced the architectural styles of subsequent South Indian dynasties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hampi** was the capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire**.
 
• **Rameshwaram** is a town in **Tamil Nadu**, known for its temple dedicated to** Lord Shiva**.
 
• **Orugallu**, also known as **Warangal**, was the capital of the **Kakatiya dynasty**.
 
• The Pallavas were known for their patronage of art and architecture, which is evident from the numerous temples and monuments they built in Kanchipuram and surrounding areas.
 
• Kanchipuram continues to be an important pilgrimage site and is often referred to as the "City of a Thousand Temples."

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science in 1876, an institution, devoted to the pursuit of fundamental research in the frontier areas of basic sciences?

• The Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science has contributed significantly to the advancement of science in India.

• **Har Gobind Khorana** was an Indian-American biochemist who won the** Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1968** for his research on the synthesis of proteins.

questions.question: The word ________ means a body of persons that looks after the implementation of rules and regulations in actual practice.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Executive**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Executive** refers to a body of persons responsible for implementing rules and regulations in actual practice.
 
• The executive branch of government is responsible for the day-to-day administration and enforcement of laws.
 
• It is distinct from the **Legislature**, which makes laws, and the **Judiciary**, which interprets laws.
 
• In most democratic systems, the executive includes the head of state (such as a president or monarch) and the head of government (such as a prime minister), along with their appointed officials and civil servants.
 
• The executive exercises authority in and holds responsibility for the governance of a state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Legislature** is the branch of government that creates laws.
 
• The **Judiciary** interprets and applies the law to ensure justice is administered.
 
• The **Bureaucracy** refers to the administrative system governing any large institution, often characterized by formal procedures and hierarchy.
 
• Understanding the distinct roles of these branches is crucial for comprehending how a government functions effectively.
